content.title: Average Speed
content.summary: Average speed uses total distance and total time.
content.formula_plain: average speed = total distance / total time
content.explanation: Average speed uses total distance and total time.
conditions: Distance and time must use compatible units.

example.question: A body covers 100 m in 20 s.

common_mistakes: Confusing average speed with average velocity.

content.title: Uniform Acceleration Equations
content.summary: Relations for one-dimensional motion with constant acceleration.
content.formula_plain: v = u + at; s = ut + ½at²; v² = u² + 2as
content.explanation: Relations for one-dimensional motion with constant acceleration.
common_mistakes: Using equations for variable acceleration.

content.title: Newton’s Second Law
content.summary: Net force equals rate of change of momentum.
content.formula_plain: F = dp/dt; for constant mass F = ma
content.explanation: Net force equals rate of change of momentum.
conditions: F is net force; vectors require direction.

example.question: A 2 kg body accelerates at 3 m/s².

common_mistakes: Using one force instead of net force.

content.title: Kinetic Energy
content.explanation: Energy due to motion.
common_mistakes: Forgetting the square on speed.

content.title: Work by a Constant Force
content.summary: Work is the component of force along displacement multiplied by displacement.
content.explanation: Work is the component of force along displacement multiplied by displacement.
content.when_to_use: Use for constant force and straight displacement.
conditions: Work can be negative or zero.

example.question: F=10 N, s=2 m, same direction.

common_mistakes: Using F s without the angle factor.

content.title: Gravitational Potential Energy Near Earth
content.summary: Potential energy relative to a chosen reference level near Earth’s surface.
content.explanation: Potential energy relative to a chosen reference level near Earth’s surface.
content.when_to_use: Use for small height changes near Earth.

example.question: m=2 kg, g=10 m/s², h=3 m.

common_mistakes: Confusing height with path length.

content.title: Escape Speed
content.summary: Minimum speed needed to escape a spherical body without further propulsion, neglecting atmosphere and rotation.
content.explanation: Minimum speed needed to escape a spherical body without further propulsion, neglecting atmosphere and rotation.
content.when_to_use: Use for ideal escape from a spherical body.

example.question: For g=10 m/s² and R=6.4×10⁶ m, estimate vₑ.

common_mistakes: Confusing escape speed with orbital speed.

content.title: Pressure
content.summary: Pressure is normal force per unit area.
content.explanation: Pressure is normal force per unit area.
content.when_to_use: Use for force distributed over an area.
conditions: Force must be normal to area for this simple form.
common_mistakes: Using length instead of area.

content.title: First Law of Thermodynamics
content.summary: Heat supplied equals increase in internal energy plus work done by the system.
content.explanation: Heat supplied equals increase in internal energy plus work done by the system.
content.when_to_use: Use with the stated sign convention.

example.question: If ΔQ=100 J and W=30 J, find ΔU.

common_mistakes: Reversing work sign conventions.

content.title: Time Period of a Simple Pendulum
content.summary: Time period of a simple pendulum for small angular oscillations.
keywords: time period of a simple pendulum
content.explanation: Time period of a simple pendulum for small angular oscillations.
conditions: Small angle approximation; independent of bob mass.

example.question: How does T change if l becomes four times?

common_mistakes: Including bob mass in the formula.

content.title: Permutations
content.summary: Counts ordered selections of r objects from n distinct objects.
content.explanation: Counts ordered selections of r objects from n distinct objects.
common_mistakes: Using combinations when order matters.

content.title: Combinations
content.explanation: Counts unordered selections.
content.when_to_use: Use when order does not matter.
common_mistakes: Confusing selection with arrangement.

content.title: Binomial General Term
content.summary: General term in the expansion of (a+b)^n.
content.explanation: General term in the expansion of (a+b)^n.
content.when_to_use: Use to find a particular term.
conditions: The term number is r+1, not r.
common_mistakes: Using r equal to the displayed term number.

content.title: Sum of a Finite Geometric Progression
content.summary: Sum of the first n terms of a GP.
keywords: sum of a finite geometric progression
content.explanation: Sum of the first n terms of a GP.
content.when_to_use: Use for a finite GP with r ≠ 1.
common_mistakes: Sign error in denominator.

content.title: Mole Relationship
content.summary: Connects mass, molar mass and number of entities.
content.explanation: Connects mass, molar mass and number of entities.

example.question: How many moles are in 18 g water?

common_mistakes: Confusing molar mass with mass.

content.title: Molarity
content.summary: Molarity is moles of solute per litre of solution.
content.explanation: Molarity is moles of solute per litre of solution.
content.when_to_use: Use for concentration based on solution volume.
common_mistakes: Using solvent volume instead of solution volume.

content.title: Molality
content.summary: Molality is moles of solute per kilogram of solvent.
content.formula_plain: molality = moles of solute / mass of solvent in kg
content.explanation: Molality is moles of solute per kilogram of solvent.
content.when_to_use: Use when solvent mass is specified.
common_mistakes: Using solution mass.

content.title: Ideal Gas Equation
content.summary: Relates pressure, volume, amount and temperature for an ideal gas.
content.explanation: Relates pressure, volume, amount and temperature for an ideal gas.
content.when_to_use: Use for ideal-gas calculations; formative syllabus status should be checked.
common_mistakes: Using Celsius directly.

content.title: Gibbs Energy Relation
content.summary: Relates enthalpy, entropy and spontaneity at constant temperature and pressure.
content.explanation: Relates enthalpy, entropy and spontaneity at constant temperature and pressure.
content.when_to_use: Use for spontaneity under constant T and P.

example.question: If ΔH=10 kJ/mol, TΔS=15 kJ/mol, find ΔG.

common_mistakes: Mixing J and kJ.
